page.overview:
What is Balrogs?

The Balrogs, or Valaraukar (singular Valarauko, Quenya for "Demon of power"), were three to seven Maiar seduced and corrupted by Morgoth into betraying the Valar and serving him, turning into dreadful Úmaiar and scourges of fire cloaked in shadow. They were counted amongst Morgoth's most powerful and fearsome servants.

Originally, the Balrogs were Maiar who were persuaded by Melkor's might and splendor to betray the Valar and join his cause and corrupted by him into Úmaiar. Their first dwelling was in Utumno, the great fortress of the Iron Mountains, but after their master's defeat during the Battle of the Powers, the Balrogs and other creatures in Melkor's service escaped to Angband and hibernated there.

The Balrogs were present as early as the Years of the Trees when Melkor and Ungoliant destroyed the Two Trees of Valinor. By then, the Balrogs remained in the pits of Angband. After Melkor (now named Morgoth) fled Valinor with Ungoliant, he came to Lammoth near the ruins of Angband to renew his rule in Middle-earth. A disagreement with Ungoliant led to her attacking him, and Morgoth gave out a great cry that roused the Balrogs from their slumber. In a tempest of fire, they came and drove Ungoliant away, prepared to pursue her. However, they were halted by Morgoth and returned to Angband, which shortly thereafter was constructed anew.

When the Ñoldor won the battle Dagor-nuin-Giliath, Fëanor and a small vanguard pursued the remnants of the Orc army that had attacked them. The Elven troop came within sight of Angband, but the Orcs, who had by this point noted the small size of Fëanor's force, turned and gave battle. As the engagement had occurred so close to Angband, a number of Balrogs emerged to aid the Orcs, and they quickly slew most of the Elves. Fëanor was left to fight on alone, and for a long while he did so, despite being wounded many times. But at last Gothmog, the first Lord of Balrogs, struck Fëanor to the ground. A relief force led by Fëanor's sons soon arrived and prevented their father from being slain on the battlefield. The Balrogs returned to Angbad, and Fëanor died shortly thereafter of his wounds.
